clue.text: Function four had set in motion

parts.note: to act is to function or operate
four in Roman numerals
had a meal means ate

explanation.surface: Some device's fourth function had been switched on and set running.
explanation.definitionFit: To activate a machine or process is to start it working, the same as setting it going.

clue.text: Light sherry perhaps making wife loud

indicators.note: making one thing into another tells us to swap the named letter for a new one

parts.note: sherry is one example of a fortified wine
W is the standard abbreviation for wife
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A pale fino sherry seems to make someone's wife noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: WINE has its W changed to F, giving FINE. 'Light sherry' reads as one phrase, but 'Light' is the definition and 'sherry perhaps' the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine and light both describe something delicate, thin or slender in texture, like fine rain or light fabric.

clue.text: Poke your nose in short march heading north, getting led astray

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
something short has been cut, so the final letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a protest march is a demo

indicators.note: led astray means taken off course, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A busybody intrudes on a brief protest march heading north and is led off course.
explanation.walkthrough: DEMO loses its last letter to DEM, which reads upwards as MED; LED shuffled becomes DLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to interfere in other people's business, which the idiom poke your nose in also describes.

clue.text: On top of church, university's consumed by, for one, Laurel and Hardy

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting above another comes first in the entry
something consumed by another is swallowed up inside it

parts.note: Stan Laurel is one example of a Stan
U is the abbreviation for university
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: The comedy duo Laurel and Hardy are pictured on a church roof, munching through a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laurel and Hardy' reads as the famous double act, but only Laurel is wordplay; 'Hardy' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Staunch can mean sturdy and strongly built, so it is a synonym of hardy in the sense of robust and tough.

clue.text: Clumsiness of Putin tied to corrupt base

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or debased, so these letters are twisted out of shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A political jibe at the Russian leader's bungling and his links to a crooked military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a military site or an adjective for low, but here it is the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineptitude is lack of skill or competence, so it is a synonym for awkward clumsiness in action.

clue.text: Order comic Jack to pack in career occasionally

indicators.note: packing something in means stuffing it inside a container

parts.note: Jack Dee is a British stand-up comedian

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so just every other letter is kept

parts.note: the odd-placed letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone orders the comedian Jack Dee to quit his career now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack in' suggests giving up, but here it means stuff inside. Jack Dee is a deadpan British comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official order or command issued by an authority, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Maybe collision investigator flips, constrained by stress

indicators.note: something constrained by another is held within it

parts.note: stress on a syllable is its accent

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way round

parts.note: a DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A road-crash investigator cracks under the pressure of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: DI, a Detective Inspector, is the standard crossword investigator.
explanation.definitionFit: A collision is one example of an accident, hence 'maybe' signalling the definition by example.

clue.text: Focus of Tommy Fury — to find place to feed

indicators.note: the focus of a word is its centre, so only its middle letter is used

parts.note: the central letter of the five-letter name
fury is intense anger

explanation.surface: Boxer Tommy Fury's single-minded rage drives him to find somewhere to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Fury is a British boxer; his name splits into the middle of Tommy and a synonym for fury.
explanation.definitionFit: A manger is the trough from which horses or cattle eat their fodder in a stable.

clue.text: Mixture the French brought about to stop irritating condition for boxer?

indicators.note: stopping something up means plugging a gap inside it

parts.note: mange is a skin disease of dogs, and a boxer is a breed of dog

indicators.note: bringing a ship about turns it round to face the other way

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A French treatment is applied to soothe a fighter's itchy skin complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' looks like a fighter, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A melange is a varied blend or medley of different things, so it means a mixture.

clue.text: Square or fashionable to visit Geordieland?

definitions.note: the answer is a number that is a square, not the noun square itself

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside the place visited

parts.note: Geordies come from Newcastle in North East England, abbreviated NE
something in is fashionable

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone old-fashioned or trendy should head to Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' wants to mean old-fashioned, the opposite of fashionable, but it is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine equals three times three, making it a perfect square in arithmetic.

clue.text: Reversing hit back of truck after large drink and place car illegally

indicators.note: one piece placed after another follows it in the entry

parts.note: a double is a large measure of spirits

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: to rap is to strike or hit

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A drunk driver backs into a lorry and leaves the car parked where it shouldn't be.
explanation.walkthrough: RAP reversed is PAR; DOUBLE comes first, then PAR and K.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-park is to leave a vehicle alongside one already parked at the kerb, blocking traffic and breaking the law.

clue.text: Countenance going around Asda on a regular basis for show

indicators.note: one word going around another wraps it inside

parts.note: countenance is a person's face

indicators.note: regularly spaced letters are taken, skipping every other one

parts.note: the first and third letters of the supermarket name

explanation.surface: A shopper regularly visits the Asda supermarket simply to be seen there.
explanation.walkthrough: Asda is a British supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A facade is an outward appearance put on for show, a false front hiding the real situation.

clue.text: Person selling United in move over European on returning

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed over another comes before it
one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a move or step taken is an action
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names
E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word runs the other way

parts.note: re means on, as in regarding

explanation.surface: A Manchester United player is transferred to a European club as he heads home.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the European before what follows; 'on' is the preposition meaning regarding.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer is the person who conducts a sale of goods by taking bids, so is someone selling.

clue.text: Innocent, I'm excused pinching piece of old French bread

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing a small part, so the letters are lifted from inside the words

parts.note: found running across the words

explanation.surface: Someone protests innocence and is let off for stealing a loaf in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, not a loaf. The centime was a hundredth of the old French franc.
explanation.definitionFit: A centime was a small coin of the pre-euro French currency, and bread is slang for money.

clue.text: Entertainer in camp lefty film

parts.note: a left-winger or socialist is a red
a film or thin layer is a coat

explanation.surface: Reads like a review of a flamboyant left-wing movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' looks like the flamboyant adjective. A Redcoat is an entertainer at a Butlin's holiday camp in Britain, named for their red jackets.
explanation.definitionFit: Butlin's holiday camps employ staff in red jackets to host games and shows, called redcoats.

clue.text: Entertaining before lunch — exhausting

parts.note: a.m. means the morning, the time before lunch
exhausting a supply means using it up

explanation.surface: Hosting guests before lunch proves tiring work.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusing and entertaining are synonymous adjectives describing something that gives pleasure or makes people laugh.

clue.text: Nonplussed seeing flightless birds in the hay

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: to hit the hay is to go to bed
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled to find ostrich-like birds lying in the hay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the hay' is the idiom 'hit the hay', meaning in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemused and nonplussed both describe being puzzled, confused and unsure how to react.

clue.text: Clearance of electronic vehicle lacking force fake news

parts.note: E for electronic and V for vehicle, as in an EV

indicators.note: lacking something means going without it, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: made-up news is fiction
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: Reads like a headline about clearing out an electric car accused of spreading disinformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clearance' suggests tidying up, but it means turning people out of a home.
explanation.definitionFit: An eviction is the forced removal of tenants from a property, a clearance of its occupants.

clue.text: Reform ask peer to be impartial politician

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A call for a member of the Lords to stay neutral during political reform.
explanation.definitionFit: The Speaker presides over the House of Commons and must stay neutral between parties once elected.

clue.text: Almost nervous after endless mickey-taking, in steep decline

indicators.note: one piece coming after another follows it in the entry
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: a skit is a parody that takes the mickey, British slang for mocks

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter is removed

parts.note: jumpy means nervous and on edge

explanation.surface: Someone becomes anxious after endless teasing and their mood falls sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIT and JUMPY each lose their last letter. 'Decline' looks like a drop in mood, but it means a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski jump is a steeply inclined ramp down which skiers race before launching into the air.

clue.text: Minor runner's right to plug possible source of energy

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so the piece is pushed inside the other

parts.note: steam can drive engines and turbines
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A junior athlete is entitled to plug into a power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' wants to be an athlete; it is a running watercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a small river, a minor body of running water, so a little runner in crossword terms.

clue.text: Refer to work from the East that's lyrical

indicators.note: in an across entry coming from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: to cite a source is to refer to it
op, opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Mentioning a piece of writing from Asia that is full of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic and lyrical both describe expressive, imaginative language with the qualities of verse.

clue.text: Introduce Spooner's complimentary photos

indicators.note: Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds are exchanged

parts.note: complimentary photos are free pics; swap the opening sounds of those two words

explanation.surface: An instruction to present a famous don's flattering snapshots.
explanation.walkthrough: Complimentary here means given free, not flattering, which is what the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefix something is to put it at the front or before, introducing it ahead of the rest.

clue.text: In RAF, Ange Postecoglou's first exercises bringing sweet reward?

indicators.note: exercising works things over and moves them about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: first points at the opening letter of the name only

parts.note: the opening letter of the football manager's surname

explanation.surface: Football manager Ange Postecoglou puts his team through drills with the air force, then earns a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a linking preposition, but its letters are part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Frangipane is a sweet almond cream used in tarts and pastries, the sort of treat given as a reward.

clue.text: Figures Prada tailor-makes bags

indicators.note: to bag something is to hold it, so the letters sit enclosed inside the words

parts.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: The fashion house Prada makes bespoke handbags to fit customers' figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' suggests body shapes for a tailor, but it means numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and statistics, often numerical, so figures in the sense of numbers collected for analysis.

clue.text: Day bolstered by a quiet scotch

indicators.note: in a down entry something propped up from below sits above what supports it

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day
taken as written
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A day's spirits are lifted by a peaceful glass of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky, but it is the verb meaning to put an end to.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch hopes or rumours is to dash them, destroying or stamping them out completely.

clue.text: Villain's request to hide publicity early sign of guilt

indicators.note: something hidden is tucked away inside something else

parts.note: to beg is to request earnestly
an ad is a piece of publicity

indicators.note: the earliest sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A criminal begs to keep his notoriety quiet, the first hint that he did it.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad egg is an idiom for a dishonest or untrustworthy person, a rogue or scoundrel.

clue.text: Release of energy by young lady, one working

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
miss is the title for a young unmarried woman
I is the Roman numeral one
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A young woman at work gives off a burst of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Release of energy' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Release' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An emission is the act of giving off or discharging something such as gas, light or heat.
